ares_pc.releaseNotes:
ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy. 

Additionally, there have been many updates to the core ares application across all platforms. Per-core input configuration has been added, updated video, audio, & input drivers are available, bug fixes, additional options have been added, and core dependencies have been updated. 

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

 - CD-ROM: implement behavior where a new command cannot be executed until pending       
 - CD-ROM: implement 'command/parameter busy' register
 - DMA: improve chopping/allowing the cpu to run between blocks of a long transfer
 - DMA: fixed incorrect bit position for DMA channel chopping enable
 - DMA: fixed block DMA using incorrect timing
 - DMA: fixed SPU canReadDMA/canWriteDMA flags
 - MDEC: implement basic decode timing
 - MDEC: implement correct input fifo behavior
 - MDEC: fix behavior when an incomplete block is transferred via the input fifo
 - MDEC: fix DMA request registers, input/output full/empty registers, busy register
 - GPU: use correct clock frequency for PAL and NTSC
 - GPU: fix hblank timing
 - GPU: Fixed some clocking issues
 - Timer: improve behavior around timer overflow/target reached IRQ

**Nintendo - Game Boy Advance**

 - Only trigger keypad IRQ when input changes
 - Fixed handling of repeat bit during immediate DMA transfers
 - Prefetcher should fail reading across 128KiB boundaries
 - OBJ mosaic fixes to correct some graphical bugs
 - Prevent instruction tracing from modifying open bus
 - Refactored bus reads fixing some open bus edge cases
 - Implemented internal horizontal/vertical window flags when window boundaries reached
 - Improved affine parameter timings
 - Fixed wave RAM bank selection
 - Added OAM to memory viewer
 - Implemented OAM stage timings for sprite rendering

**Nintendo - Super Famicom / SNES**

 - Added support for loading GBC games in the Super Game Boy
 - Super Game Boy accuracy fixes (multiplayer, packet acknowledgement, register mirroring)
 - Improved auto-joypad polling accuracy

**Nintendo - Nintendo 64**

 - CPU & RSP JIT improvements resulting in improved performance 
 - Cubivore (Doubutsu Banchou w/English patch applied) support added

Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)

armsx3.releaseNotes: # ARMSX3 1.2 ## Remote play - **Play a friend's game as player 2.** Their game streams to your device and you play with your own controller or the touch controls. Only the stream runs on your side, so you don't need the game. - **On the same Wi-Fi or online.** On the same Wi-Fi, friends hosting a game show up by themselves. Online, the host gets a six-character code to send you. If the code service can't be reached, you and your friend can send each other invite messages to paste instead. - **To host:** start a game, open the in-game menu, tap Friends, then Host on this Wi-Fi or Invite online. **To join:** open Remote play from the game library menu. - **The host lets each friend in.** When someone connects, the game pauses and the host accepts or declines them. Nothing streams until they say yes. - **Direct connection.** The stream goes straight between the two devices, with no server in between, so how well it plays depends on both connections and how far apart you are. Online, the host's router is asked to open a port for the session when it supports that, which helps friends on networks that block incoming connections. - **Player 2 feels the game's rumble**, and the host sees a message when a friend joins or leaves. - **For the player joining:** an exit button, your touch controls with your own layout and skin, stream stats, and a Wi-Fi QoS marking option to try on networks that sort traffic. - Hosting needs the Vulkan renderer. copperline_pc.releaseNotes:
Copperline 1.0.0 is the first stable release. It follows two weeks of testing of 1.0.0-rc.1 and is the 23rd release since the source went public on 14 June.

This release adds Smart framing and native 1:1 screenshots, more control over where and how the window opens, VHD hard-disk images, a fix for AGA sprites that use scan-doubling, and a Check for updates button that only contacts GitHub when you press it.

## Copperline 1.0 at a glance

- **Machines:** A1000, A500, A500+, A600, A1200, A3000, A4000, CDTV and CD32, with OCS, ECS and AGA chipsets and 68000 to 68060 CPUs, FPUs and MMUs.
- **Accuracy:** the CPU and custom chips run on one colour-clock timeline, with the chip bus shared out cycle by cycle. Timing is checked against a real A1200, A4000 and CD32, and 45 test programs are compared pixel for pixel on every change.
- **Ready to run:** the open AROS ROM is bundled, as are ROMs for the A2091, A4091 and IDE boards, the CD32 FMV module and the HRTMon freezer. WHDLoad packages and Amiga programs boot directly.
- **Media and expansion:** floppy images including IPF and SCP, real drives through a Greaseweazle, IDE and SCSI hard disks, CDs, host folders, RTG graphics cards, Ethernet, `bsdsocket.library` without a TCP/IP stack, and built-in MT-32 (with your own ROMs) and General MIDI synthesizers.
- **Playing:** save states, rewind, run-ahead, CRT shaders and a 1084 monitor front, gamepads, and rollback netplay for up to four players with up to eight spectators.
- **Developing:** a debugger beside the live display with reverse stepping, a frame analyzer, GDB, VS Code source debugging, profiling, a control protocol and an MCP server.
- **Everywhere:** macOS, Windows and Linux builds, a [browser version](https://copperline.dev/try/) and a RetroArch core.

The [manual](https://copperline.dev/docs/) covers all of it.

## Before upgrading

- **macOS 14.2 or newer is required, and the app now says so.** Copperline has needed macOS 14.2 since 0.16.0 because of the Core Audio functions it uses, but the app declared 11.0, so older systems launched it and it crashed. macOS now refuses to open it with the standard "requires a newer version of macOS" message. Homebrew requires Sonoma.
- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files from 0.20.0, 0.21.0 and 1.0.0-rc.1 still load.
- **Volume is no longer saved in save states.** Loading a state, rewinding, run-ahead and netplay rollback now keep your current volume, mono and stereo settings and audio filter choice.
- **The window title has changed.** By default it now shows the version, machine and boot ROM, and no longer includes the git commit. Window-manager rules that match the old title need updating; `[display] title` sets your own.
- **Guest writes to `$BFFF00`-`$BFFF07` now print debug output** (see below). This follows `[emulation] uaelib`, which is on by default; set it to `false` to turn off both the uaelib trap and the debug ports.

**Upgrading from 0.21.0 or earlier?** Also read the [1.0.0-rc.1 notes](https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/releases/tag/v1.0.0-rc.1). The netplay protocol changed, high-density floppy images are refused, some command-line combinations are now errors, and `--run PROG --exit-on-return` on its own runs without a window.

## Smart framing

The TV overscan setting crops the picture to roughly what a television showed, but software that placed its picture a little off-centre lost part of it at the edges. The CD32 boot logo is one example. The new **Smart** framing keeps the TV crop and moves it sideways to follow the display window the program sets up. It moves by at most eight lo-res pixels, only after the position has held for 25 frames, and stays put through blank frames, so the picture does not wander. Manual centring still works on top of it.

You need to map the analog triggers to DS buttons or special function keys first.
If your controller does not have analog triggers, or if its L2/R2 buttons generate both button events and analog trigger events at the same time (which may cause mapped buttons to be triggered twice), it is recommended to disable this option.

Decide the rotation mode of the left and right analog sticks on the controller.

A new option allows the DS bottom screen to be shown by default when using single-screen layouts.
If your dual-screen handheld gaming device has the bottom screen as the main screen, it is highly recommended to enable this option for a better screen-swap experience.

gse_speedrun.releaseNotes:
Sixth release of GSE.

This release replaces the GBA emulation core. Previously, [mGBA's](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba) GBA emulation core was used for GBA games. GSE now uses [Mesen's](https://github.com/nesdev-org/MesenCE) GBA emulation core for GBA games. This offers far better accuracy, to the point even GBA Pokémon TASes can sync on console, and as such emulator players can fairly compete with console players in GBA Pokémon speedrunners, along with likely many other games.

This release also features various bugfixes, along with minor QoL improvements such as an option to automatically hide the mouse cursor, saving the last used emulator width/height for when no ROM is loaded (i.e. no longer hardcoding GBA resolution), and more.

This release will likely be the last release for various old platforms (for macOS < 12, Linux < glibc 2.35, and Android < 7), mainly due to dependencies dropping support. This shouldn't affect most users, but it is noted for whatever users still use these old platforms.

Several download options are available, for various OSes and CPU architectures, per the [requirements listed in the README](https://github.com/CasualPokePlayer/GSE/blob/v0.6/README.md#user-requirements). # KytyPlus v4.3 Release Notes

KytyPlus v4.3 collects launcher compatibility, Vulkan shader, and Windows path-handling fixes made since v4.1. These changes improve specific code paths and do not imply a broad increase in game compatibility.

## What’s new

### Vulkan layer-output shader compatibility

- Layer-output shaders now use the core SPIR-V `ShaderLayer` capability enabled by the Vulkan feature set, rather than the unenabled `SPV_EXT_shader_viewport_index_layer` extension.
- Layer-output shaders use SPIR-V 1.5 and include their live descriptor and push-constant variables in the entry-point interface. Shaders without layer output retain SPIR-V 1.3.
- Added regression coverage for SPIR-V validation and Vulkan pipeline creation.

### Launcher and CLI configuration compatibility

- Legacy launcher configurations can disable FSR without failing because of inherited default output dimensions.
- Explicit FSR output dimensions remain validated, and invalid or incomplete dimensions are rejected.
- Fixed successful launcher process starts being reported with Qt’s misleading “Unknown error” text.
- Added emulator CLI regressions for the discussion #15 argument combination and FSR option ordering/validation.

### Windows Unicode game paths

- Mounting and resolving game paths now consistently convert UTF-8 strings to native filesystem paths on Windows.
- Windows file enumeration and directory operations preserve non-ASCII names, including paths containing characters such as an en dash.
- Added regression coverage for Unicode mount paths, guest filenames, directory opens, and file reads.

### Compatibility data

- Updated Dead Cells (`PPSA-15554`) to **Playable**, last tested with v4.1.

## Limitations

- The shader change has focused validation and regression coverage; it is not a guarantee that every game or graphics driver is compatible.

mame4droid.releaseNotes:
#  Rollback NetPlay: compatibility and stability

Rollback is what makes NetPlay feel like two people on one machine instead of
two people waiting for each other. This release is mostly about the games that
could not use it, and the sessions that fell apart halfway through.

## Street Fighter III now runs in rollback

All of CPS-3 does: 3rd Strike and the earlier two, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure,
Red Earth. Until now these were stuck in Lockstep, which is the worst place for
a fighting game to be.

The problem was size. To rewind, rollback keeps dozens of snapshots of the
machine in memory, and a CPS-3 snapshot was enormous — it carried the entire
game loaded from the CD, tens of megabytes of code, graphics and samples that
never change while you play. Snapshots now leave all of that behind and keep
only what the game actually writes to. What used to be far past any sane limit
now fits with room to spare.

Games that already fit benefit too: smaller snapshots mean less memory and less
work on every correction.

## More games run in rollback

The host now hands its machine state to the joiner by default, so games that
used to refuse rollback because both sides could not be trusted to boot
identically now qualify.

## Sessions that used to break

**Joining and resyncing.** A drop-in join or a mid-game resync would sometimes
leave one machine frozen, or the joiner on a black screen, with nothing to do
but disconnect. The snapshot was being taken wherever the emulation happened to
be at that instant, sometimes in the middle of a frame with work still pending.
It is now always taken at the end of a frame, once the video chip has finished
and the interrupt queue is drained. The state that arrives is one the other
machine can actually resume from.

**Brief network drops.** Lose enough packets in a row and one frame would stay
a guess forever: the game kept running, quietly wrong, and the two sides drifted
apart over the next minutes. That frame is now re-requested from the other
player and the session repairs itself. Tested by cutting the connection on
purpose, over and over.

**Dials, spinners and 4-way sticks.** Part of the live control state was not
included in a rollback, so analog games could jump or fall back to a stale
reading after a correction. It travels with the state now.

## Quick messages

The last release said there would be no chat, and there still isn't one. What
there is now is a short list of fixed phrases — hello, good game, wait a moment,
insert coin and press start, I have to go. Picking one sends a number, not text,
and the other player's device shows that phrase in their own language. Nothing
typed, nothing to moderate, nothing stored. You can mute the ones you receive.

## Drop-in BIOS selection

For games with several BIOS versions, the picker was starting on an arbitrary
one and, if you pressed Exit instead of choosing, it published your room anyway.
It now starts on the game's default BIOS, and Exit cancels the whole thing.

## Smaller things

- Dialogs start with a sensible button selected, so a gamepad can go through
  NetPlay without touching the screen. Disconnect is never the one selected,
  and it now sits at the bottom of the menu, away from the rest.
- The public room board shows the busiest countries on a line of its own.

## Both devices must be updated

The network protocol changed. An updated device and an old one will refuse each
other when connecting, which is deliberate: the alternative is a session that
looks fine and slowly falls apart.

nethersx2_lsfg.releaseNotes:
# v26500801 — Gameplay background-work preview

This update removes unnecessary work during ordinary gameplay with frame generation off. It keeps the Classic 3668 core, driver selection, game patches and saved settings from v26500800.

- Turning framegen off now removes its overlay and stops its twice-per-second monitor. A cold start with framegen off does not start that monitor. Enabling framegen and resolution-change recovery still start it when needed.
- Returning to a game applies OSD settings once. Later recovery checks only reload settings if the native emulator has actually changed the OSD preferences or an earlier apply failed. Older resume callbacks cannot apply settings in a newer session.
- FPS visibility and the user's all-stats-off choice remain supported. Flow stays 0.25 and artifact protection stays off. Framegen remains available on 60 Hz displays; this update does not change its saved switch position.

Install either APK over the existing Pink app without uninstalling or clearing data. FRAMEGEN and NONFRAMEGEN share the same package, signing certificate, memory cards and save states. The Daijisho connector from v26500800 remains compatible.

Automated checks cover monitor shutdown/re-enable, resolution recovery, redundant reload prevention, failed-apply retries and OSD preference repair. Both APKs pass signing, package/version, icon, settings layout and variant checks. The emulator core and FRAMEGEN LSFG library are byte-identical to v26500800.

This is a preview of specific background-work fixes, not a universal locked-60 claim. Game caps, patch compatibility, CPU/GPU load and storage activity still affect performance. Physical checks and measurement limits are recorded in the accompanying validation receipt.

On Nova, Ultimate Spider-Man launched from Daijisho with framegen off. Resolution changes in both 4:3 and widescreen, FPS ON/OFF, and restoring the current session passed. All eight existing save/card files and seven backed-up configuration files remained byte-identical; the current session was preserved in one previously empty save slot.

The initial widescreen camera-pan sample reported about 59.94 game FPS and two roughly 33 ms presentation intervals across 44 seconds, while a large SD-card transfer was active. These initial samples do not establish a clean before/after performance improvement.

Follow-up tests briefly paused the transfer and resumed it safely after each comparison. Hitches also occurred without the transfer. With framegen off, the best longer Nova sample used Sync To Host Refresh Rate, Host VSync and Threaded Presentation together: one 33.36 ms presentation interval across 109.28 seconds of camera movement in Ultimate Spider-Man at 1.5x and 4:3. Those timing settings were retained on the test Nova. A shorter zero-outlier result did not hold across longer tests, so occasional hitches remain and locked 60 is not verified. This follow-up changes only the test device settings and validation notes; the APKs and shipped defaults are unchanged. Thor, other games and sustained city traversal were not retested.

See the [validation receipt](https://github.com/slushiimusic/NetherSX2-Slushii-Turnip-Fix/blob/main/releases/v26500801-validation.json) for the sample metrics and scope.

## Misc Internal Changes
* The build system no longer prints ignored errors when building SameBoy without RGBDS installed if prebuilt boot ROMs are used
* `ibtool` no longer silently fails when building the Cocoa or iOS frontends
* The logging API now has attribute flags that mark if a log line is an error or a warning caused by the previous API call

# Release 5.8.0
*2026-10-14*
---

## Unified Windows Release (WPF + Avalonia)
- **One download for both apps** — The release zip now places `SimpleLauncher.exe` (WPF) and `SimpleLauncher.Avalonia.exe` (Avalonia) side by side with a single shared content set (`images/`, `tools/`, `samples/`, `appsettings.json`) and ships one `Updater.exe` that updates either app.
- **Shared single-instance guard** — Only one of the two apps can run at a time; launching the other brings the running instance to the foreground.
- **Updater relaunches the app that started it** — and still works on legacy WPF-only installs.

## Unified Settings Database (`settings.dat`)
- **One SQLite store for both apps** — Favorites, play history, application settings, emulator settings, per-system play times, and system configurations now live in a single `settings.dat` in `%LocalAppData%\SimpleLauncher` (or the portable folder).
- **Automatic migration** — The first launch migrates `settings.xml`, `system.xml`, `favorites.dat`, and `playhistory.dat`, verifies the result, and shelves the legacy files as `.bak`; on failure nothing is changed and the next launch retries.
- **Merge support** — If a database already exists, any remaining legacy files are merged into it without losing database-only data or duplicating entries.
- **Read-only database recovery** — A read-only `settings.dat` is detected and recovered instead of crashing; failed saves are observed and logged.
- **Cross-app consistency** — Systems renamed or deleted in one app stay in sync with favorites and play history.

## WPF: Card Size Slider
- **Top-bar slider** — Resize game thumbnails with a slider next to the view controls (debounced when dragging), kept in sync with "Set Button Size" and Ctrl+Mouse wheel zoom.

## Shared Localization
- **One JSON pack set for both apps** — The 18 language packs (2671 keys each) now live once in `SimpleLauncher.Core\Localization`; WPF embeds them as pack resources and Avalonia embeds them in its assembly.
- **Legacy XAML resources removed** — The per-language `strings.*.xaml` files are gone.
- **Avalonia message boxes fully localized**.

## Reliability & Security
- **Extraction** — Zip-Slip validation fails closed, extraction no longer wipes destination folders (only files written by the failed run are removed), partial files are cleaned up, and locked archives are retried.
- **Downloads** — User cancellation is honored promptly, downloaded file names are sanitized against path traversal, and failures retry.
- **Launching** — Launch gating, rename migration, elevation handling, and invalid/missing executable dialogs were repaired; user cancellations and invalid executables are no longer reported as bugs.
- **Xbox disc images** — xemu and Cxbx-Reloaded open Xbox games in every container the bundled SimpleXisoDrive supports: XISO (`.iso`/`.xiso`), CISO (`.cso`) and ZArchive (`.zar`) mount as virtual drives on Windows (Dokan) and Linux (FUSE 3) — xemu receives the virtual `image.iso`, Cxbx-Reloaded the mounted `default.xbe` (it cannot read a raw Xbox image); Xbox-ISO `.chd` files now prefer SimpleXisoDrive and fall back to CHDMounter when the driver is unavailable.
- **Updater** — Staged-file swap with rollback safety, path containment checks, safe restart, and retry, so a failed update no longer leaves a half-updated install.
- **Stability** — Fixed a gamepad-reconnect deadlock, a hash-pipe deadlock, a shutdown stall that left a clickable orphan tray icon, and play-history races (now serialized under lock); debug logging buffers are bounded.
- **RetroAchievements** — Hardened account handling, system-name matching, favorites/play-history sync, emulator credential injection, hashing and extraction paths. winlator_cmod.releaseNotes:
Hello!

It's been a little while, so I thought I would just give a small update on project status. 

- Winlator Cmod development continues!
- My focus on next release will either be mostly QoL. This means addressing long standing bug fixes, but more importantly, **merging and crediting improvements from other forks of Cmod from trusted developers.** Primarily I'll be focused on:
- Fixing dynamic package name paths for the gamepad implementation so that name can be changed, such as adding a ludashi benchmark version with the SDL joystick native controller support.
- Input control / touch screen control bindings bug fixes
- Minor UI improvements and enhancements
- Updating all drivers, Fex, Box64, and graphics Wrapper, following Pipetto-Crypto's advice when it comes to Streamlining and avoiding feature creep (...and avoiding pure AI code slop). 
- Improve ALSA-Reflector so audio stops cutting out after 15 minutes unless you switch to headphones.

I'm leaning on this being v13.2. A v14 Cmod should be more substantial. Ultimately I would like to overhaul how Containers are created, with a focus on something more aligned and user friendly like Gamehub, such as starting the app and choosing a Windows based executable directly in the UI, then auto creating or maintain a single container or edge case containers. This would work well with something like Per Game Fixes, or a standardized compatibility list like what's on Reddit.  

Lastly, I'm sorry I'm not good about addressing Github issues. I just have not had any time. However, it is all incredibly helpful for me; the time that I do have to spend on the next release and addressing what issues have been posted this past year (...and _cough_ Arc _cough_ raiding...). I am also looking forward to what Valve brings to the table with the Frame and it's ARM based Linux OS with Android app support. I imagine Proton is going to be getting some major improvements for ARM over the next year, so I don't see things slowing down much. Google seems to be walking back some of the unknown app restrictions they announced this year, so that's also good. Lots to look forward to. 

Stay Kazzy,
Goro Majima
_Majima Construction_

I pretty much finished my Joy-Con 2 / Nintendo Switch 2 Pro controller bluetooth driver/CLI tool for Linux systems, so I can get back to Winlator/PC Emulation on Android in general.

# X360 Mobile 0.6.3 and X360 Companion 0.1.0

X360 Mobile 0.6.3 introduces local wireless multiplayer through the new X360
Companion application, alongside Android Home shortcuts, a clearer driver
catalog and a unified touch-control system.

## X360 Companion 0.1.0

- Added X360 Companion, a separate Android application that turns a phone on
  the same local network or a paired Bluetooth device into a remote XInput
  controller.
- Up to three companions can be assigned independently to P2, P3 or P4. P1
  remains protected from remote assignment unless the host explicitly enables
  remote-only play.
- Added user-confirmed pairing, trusted-host management, connection recovery,
  per-player rumble and GamerProfile selection on the host.
- Added a shared, localized touch-control editor with compatible TOML
  import/export, presets, Xbox player indicator and controller artwork.
- LAN gameplay was validated between Odin3 and Honor through Gears of War 2.
  Bluetooth remains experimental and device-dependent.

## Library, shortcuts and input

- Added per-game Android Home shortcuts. A shortcut uses a title image embedded
  in supported game content when available, opens the direct-game loading
  screen, applies the game's saved settings and returns to the launcher when
  the game exits.
- Unified the host and Companion touch artwork, layout model and edge-aware
  factory placement. Standard layouts now preserve intended controls that
  extend partially beyond a screen edge on every supported aspect ratio.
- Expanded the integrated driver catalog with release descriptions so users can
  review maintainer compatibility notes before downloading a driver.

## Packages

- **X360 Mobile:** `emu.x360mobile.com`, version `0.6.3` (`versionCode 6039000`),
  asset `x360-mobile-0.6.3.apk`.
- **X360 Companion:** `emu.x360mobile.controller`, version `0.1.0`
  (`versionCode 11002`), asset `x360-companion-0.1.0.apk`.

Both APKs are signed with the established X360 Mobile Release identity. The
emulator uses APK Signature Scheme v3 with a local v4 sidecar; the Companion
also includes v2 for Android 8-12 compatibility.

X360 Mobile remains experimental software. It is not affiliated with Microsoft
or Xbox and must be used only with games and content the user legally owns.

# Xenra 0.4.0

[![Patreon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Patreon-Support_on_Patreon-FF424D?style=for-the-badge&logo=patreon)](https://www.patreon.com/cw/Xanite/membership)

**Xenra 0.4.0** brings a main-thread responsiveness pass, custom Vulkan driver support for Exynos (Mali) devices, experimental temporal frame generation, FATX save streaming, and the consolidation of Xenra into a single free build.

---

## Upgrade Notice

* **Install Direct:** Install Xenra 0.4.0 directly over your existing Green installation. Do not uninstall first, or your configurations, profiles, and shader caches will be deleted.
* **Gold Edition Discontinued:** Gold is retired as of 0.4.0. Installing Green (`Ali.Xanite.green`) will install alongside Gold. Gold data remains intact on your device, but a one-time setup (selecting BIOS, game paths, and granting storage permissions) is required on Green.

---

## Highlights

### Interface & Responsiveness
* **Touch & D-Pad Navigation:** Touch target resolution defers to `ACTION_UP` without walking full view trees. D-pad navigation eliminates ~170 filesystem probes per press for instant library scrolling.
* **Background Log Parsing:** `xe.log` parsing, crash log checks, and tombstone reads moved completely off the main thread across Library and Settings screens.
* **Game Data & HUD:** Directory walks for save folders and CPU/thermal reads for the performance HUD sample on dedicated background lanes without UI stutter.
* **Zero-Allocation Animations:** Glow view animators use quantized, lifecycle-bound cached gradients, eliminating continuous vsync memory allocations.
* **Cold Start Optimization:** IPC permission round-trips collapsed from 5 down to 1, and `/proc/self/maps` parsing moved to a background thread.

### Core Fixes & Memory
* **FATX Save Import Streaming:** Save imports stream in 1 MiB chunks instead of allocating full RAM. Files exceeding the 4 GiB FATX limit are cleanly rejected prior to transfer.
* **JIT Lock & Leak Fix:** Flash writes during hint cache auto-saves no longer hold `mmap_lock` (eliminating mid-game micro-stalls), and a ~3 MB session memory leak was resolved.
* **Boot & Lifecycle Guarding:** Synchronized texture adoption inside render locks to stop black/wrong frame flashes on boot, and prevented double-loads on orientation change.
* **Clean Exits:** Suppressed benign SDL thread teardown alerts on application exit, eliminating phantom "Xenra crashed" toasts.

### Custom GPU Drivers & Frame Generation
* **Exynos (Mali) Support:** Custom Vulkan driver loading is no longer gated by Qualcomm KGSL checks (`/dev/kgsl-3d0`). Mali devices (`/dev/mali`) can now load community driver ZIPs and per-game overrides.
* **Temporal Motion Prediction:** Added an experimental motion vector prediction mode (default off) to stabilize frame generation during fast pans and flat terrain. Toggle live via ADB without restarting:
  `adb shell setprop debug.xanite.fg_temporal_pred 1` (1 = On, 0 = Off)
* **Driver Card UI:** Simplified the GPU driver card to display active runtime driver status without running log parsing operations.

### Netplay & UI Polish
* **Netplay Transport Bootstrap:** Fixed HTTPS transport initialization to bootstrap automatically at boot rather than requiring the diagnostic screen.
* **Cleaned Xbox OG Context Menu:** Context menus for Original Xbox games display only relevant options (`Set Game Folder`), hiding Xbox 360-specific storage entries.

---

## Build Details

Signed with the official Xenra release key (`527f6eb59054f9b0a4f8c661f9b78a9fe80cf4a9ffaff43e0a3727b16226446f`).

| Package Name | Build APK | Version Code |
| :--- | :--- | :---: |
| `Ali.Xanite.green` | `Xenra-0.4.0-green-release.apk` | `31` |
